_meta.scope: Private or not-separately-reported US grocers that compete with Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM)
_meta.rules: Every figure has a source id (see each company's 'sources'). null = not found in a credible source. 'estimate' = third-party figure, not disclosed by the company. Nothing here was calculated by us, except where marked 'derived' (sums of quarterly numbers the company disclosed).
_meta.reliability_scale: A = company statement or filing; B = reputable trade press reporting company data; C = third-party estimate (panel data, rankings, store-locator scrapes); D = low-quality or single local report

companies.name: Trader Joe's
companies.product_focus: Small-box specialty grocer selling a tight, mostly own-brand range (snacks, frozen, prepared, produce, wine) at moderate prices; not organic-led, novelty and private label are the draw.

skus_per_store.note: No company figure found. ~4,000 items (Wikipedia) vs 2,500-3,000 (Supermarket News, outside estimates). Per Supermarket News, the company only confirms 'more than 800' private-label products.

private_label.basis: share of sales, Numerator panel, trailing 12 months to ~Dec 2024
private_label.other_cited: ~80% of items carry TJ brand names (widely repeated; attributed to the company podcast, not verified)

us_store_count.plans: ~30 stores listed as 'coming soon' across 16 states as of Oct 2026, no dates given (Supermarket News / Fox, Oct 20-21 2026).

revenue_estimate.note: No credible current estimate. NRF/Kantar 2026 Top 100 counts Trader Joe's inside Aldi ($58.36B, 2025). Older press figures of '$16B+' have no source.

sales_per_sqft.note: Often described as the highest in US grocery (BusinessWeek, 2008), but no credible current number.

companies.name: Aldi US
companies.product_focus: Hard discounter: limited range, >90% Aldi-exclusive brands, lowest-price positioning; growing fresh and organic (SimplyNature), but price comes first.

skus_per_store.note: No company figure found. Trade and press figures conflict (1,300 / ~1,400 / ~1,600 / ~1,800). Do not show a single number.

private_label.basis: Company FAQ: 'more than 90 percent of the products in our stores are ALDI exclusive brands' (seen in search results; fetching the FAQ directly redirected to an empty help page)

history.note: single secondary report, not found in an Aldi release

openings.value: plan >180 in 31 states, including ~80 Southeastern Grocers conversions

us_store_count.plans: 800 new stores 2024-2028, ~3,200 stores by end-2028; $9B US investment through 2028; >200 Winn-Dixie/Harveys conversions by end-2027; entering Maine (40th state) and Colorado (50+ stores).

avg_store_sqft.note: Only a local report (~22,000 sq ft average, Jacksonville Daily Record, Jun 2026) and older trade figures (~12,000 sq ft of selling space). Not used.

revenue_estimate.caveat: NRF/Kantar estimate that INCLUDES Trader Joe's (Aldi Nord) and the acquired Winn-Dixie/Harveys stores. NRF says its figures are estimated and may not match filings.

companies.margins_comps_disclosed: None disclosed. The company says about 1 in 3 US households shopped at Aldi in the past year and 17M new customers visited in 2025 (its own data).

companies.name: Whole Foods Market
companies.owner: Amazon.com, Inc. (since Aug 2017); not a reported segment
companies.product_focus: Large-format natural and organic supermarket with strict ingredient standards (~500 banned ingredients) at premium prices; private label '365 by Whole Foods Market' is the value tier; adding small 'Daily Shop' urban stores.

skus_per_store.note: Not disclosed. Related figure: prices were cut on more than 1,000 private-label products in the past year (Modern Retail, Sep 2025).

private_label.note: The only figure found is ~15% of revenue, from 2017 (around the acquisition). Too old; not used.

latest.as_of: 2026 (Fast Facts page, undated; 568 in total including 12 UK + 12 Canada)

us_store_count.plans: Amazon (Jan 27 2026): >100 new Whole Foods stores over the next few years; closing all Amazon Go and Amazon Fresh stores, converting some into Whole Foods. Daily Shop: 8 locations (May 2026), Boston, Chicago and Philadelphia next.

avg_store_sqft.note: Last figure ~40,000 gross sq ft (2017, via Statista); too old. Daily Shop stores are much smaller.

amazon_physical_stores_segment.caveat: Amazon's 'Physical stores' line = sales where the customer picks items in a store. It INCLUDES Amazon Fresh, Amazon Go and other Amazon-branded stores, and EXCLUDES Whole Foods orders placed online for delivery or pickup (those are in 'Online stores'). It is the best public stand-in for Whole Foods, but it is not Whole Foods. Fresh and Go close from 2026, so the line will move closer to Whole Foods-only going forward.
amazon_physical_stores_segment.annual_basis: derived = sum of the four quarters in Amazon's quarterly earnings releases (supplemental 'Net sales' table). It should match the 10-K product-group table, but the 10-K PDF could not be read here; check before publishing.

revenue_estimate.note: No separate Whole Foods revenue. Amazon says Whole Foods sales have grown 'over 40%' since the 2017 acquisition (Jan 2026).

companies.margins_comps_disclosed: None. Amazon does not report Whole Foods profit or same-store sales.

companies.name: H-E-B
companies.product_focus: Full-line conventional supermarket chain (Texas + northern Mexico) with strong fresh and prepared food and a deep own-brand program (H-E-B, Hill Country Fare value tier); competes on price and service; also runs the upscale Central Market and Mi Tienda banners.

private_label.basis: Numerator, trailing 12 months to ~Dec 2024 (Chain Store Age reported 32% of sales volume from the same report)

latest.scope: Texas AND Mexico combined (no US-only split in the boilerplate)

history.value: 465 in one release; other Feb-Jun 2026 releases say 460

us_store_count.plans: Ongoing Dallas-Fort Worth expansion (Rockwall, Forney, Irving, Murphy, Hurst openings 2025-26); $700M supply-chain investment announced May 2026.

companies.name: Erewhon
companies.owner: Private (Antoci family; Clearlake Capital minority stake reported 2023)
companies.product_focus: Ultra-premium organic and wellness market in Southern California; cafes and tonic bars take ~30% of floor space; prepared foods + private label ~40% of revenue (2021 interview); the highest price positioning in this set.

private_label.note: Prepared foods + private label together were ~40% of revenue (Tony Antoci, 2021 interview, via LA Times Jan 2025). This is not a private-label share on its own.

latest.note: Thousand Oaks = 14th location; the Pacific Palisades store closed after the Jan 2025 fire (reopening planned)

us_store_count.plans: Downtown LA (Jun 2027), Costa Mesa (Sep 2027), Palisades reopening; NYC Tonic Bar (not a grocery store).

revenue_estimate.note: The company declines to share financials (LA Times). Data-aggregator estimates are not credible.

sales_per_sqft.note: LA Times credits LA Business Journal and a 2019 Forbes item; the period and basis (annual vs weekly) are unclear, and other outlets misquote it as weekly. Show only as 'reported'.

companies.name: The Fresh Market
companies.owner: Cencosud S.A. (Chile, listed): 67% since 2022, 100% since 3Q25 (bought Apollo's 33% for $295M). Reported as Cencosud's 'United States' segment.
companies.product_focus: Upscale specialty supermarket (mostly in the Southeast) focused on fresh produce, premium meat and seafood, bakery and prepared foods; not organic-first; premium price positioning.

history.note: Grocery Dive citing the company website, after 2 closures; conflicts with the count from releases

us_store_count.plans: A WSOC-TV headline mentions a push to 200 stores by 2031; the article could not be read, so this is unconfirmed.

avg_store_sqft.note: Individual new stores ~27,000-29,000 sq ft (Reston, Falls Church); no fleet average.

revenue_estimate.basis: Cencosud segment reporting, via The Shelby Report
revenue_estimate.note: Cencosud reports the segment in CLP: 3Q25 revenue CLP 490,652M, +5.1% y/y in USD.

margins_comps_disclosed.note: YES: disclosed by the parent, Cencosud (USA segment)

3Q26.reliability: B (secondary report of Cencosud's 3Q26 release; check against the original)

companies.name: Lidl US
companies.product_focus: Hard discounter with a bigger box than Aldi: ~3,300 core items, ~80% private label, in-store bakery and rotating non-food; price-first, East Coast only.

skus_per_store.basis: core items, excluding seasonal; CEO Joel Rampoldt, PLMA keynote Nov 2025 (cut from ~4,500)

us_store_count.plans: 'Modest' growth focused on existing markets (NYC metro, DC, Atlanta).

avg_store_sqft.note: Original prototype 36,000 gross / 21,000 selling sq ft (2017); newer stores ~25,000-27,000 sq ft; no fleet average.

revenue_estimate.note: Not in the NRF 2026 Top 100; no credible estimate found.

companies.margins_comps_disclosed: None. Only Placer.ai foot-traffic gains, Jan-Aug 2026.
